question: Protocol-19 native Linux host capacity and current CPU hotspots, without optimizing the host
sourcePolicy: Fetch origin/main immediately before AWS launch; record exact commit and merge states of PRs 111 and 112
topology: Ubuntu 24.04 x86-64, same AZ, private game traffic, separate security groups
world: Unmodified HostConfig defaults, seed 7, maxClients=N, bots=0, botThreads=0; default dt and default seat-sized official world

confirmation.selection: Largest sweep N meeting criterion b

profiles.counts: 500 and largest criterion-b N if different

thresholds.b: excess p99 <= 10 ms and zero newly deferred ticks
thresholds.c: Observed sweep N where world time falls behind; publish executed ticks, deferrals and start/end world lag

timing: All post-setup frame receipts in hold: receipt milliseconds minus summed elapsed headers, minimum-normalized separately for each connection within the hold. Own-update gaps require both receipts in hold. Pooled and per-client exact nearest-rank quantiles. No timer-stall masking.
generatorValidity: Report each process CPU, total CPU out of 16 cores, poll and steering lateness, decode errors and time-weighted populations; shard further if CPU approaches saturation
exclusions: Failed or incomplete attempts retained, labelled, excluded from capacity thresholds. No mature/clustered/boosting/slow-reader claims. No mechanical fit or optimization; held-out fitting validation inapplicable.
cleanup: Terminate own instances, cancel own Spot requests, delete own key and security groups, verify zero account nonterminated instances/volumes/addresses/snapshots/open Spot requests in eu-central-1; save before/after credit-plan state privately
